rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for saying that there is not any of something, as in 冇人.

example.english: There’s no one at the door.

rows.note: Use this for something being disallowed or impossible, including notices such as ‘no smoking’ and ‘no parking’.

example.english: You can’t smoke here; no smoking is allowed.
example.jyutping: nei1 dou6 m4 ho2 ji5 sik6 jin1

rows.note: Use this before a noun when there is hardly any of it, as in 冇乜時間 ‘hardly any time’.

example.english: We have hardly any time to eat—no time for a proper meal.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 mou5 mat1 si4 gaan3 sik6 faan6

rows.meaning: not really; not a proper X
rows.note: Use this when saying that someone or something is not really or properly an example of the noun, as in 唔係傻 ‘no fool’.

example.english: I’m no expert, so I don’t want to say anything rash.
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 zyun1 gaa1 m4 gam2 lyun6 gong2
